title: Interactive on-call checklist wizard with telemetry-guided branching and safe-fallbacks
author: Elena Park
description:
Problem: on-call responders often run the same set of checks but diverge based on telemetry signals (high error-rate vs traffic spike vs degraded DB). Existing runbooks are linear and require manual decision-making, which slows time-to-detection and increases cognitive load. Goal: add an interactive checklist 'wizard' that branches based on live telemetry heuristics, surfaces the most-likely mitigation steps first, and offers safe automated scaffolding (diagnostic snapshots, canary rollbacks, and a minimal remediation runner) while preserving manual control and audit logs.

What this PR adds: an interactive, stepwise checklist component and backend orchestration that: 1) ingests a short telemetry fingerprint (SLO deltas, p95 latency change, error-rate spike) and selects the most-relevant checklist path; 2) surfaces decision hints (why this branch was chosen, confidence score, link to top traces and sample logs); 3) enables one-click diagnostic snapshot collection and ephemeral sandbox runs of safe mitigation scripts; 4) includes a safety gate that requires explicit confirmation and rate-limits automated actions; 5) logs every step to the incident timeline and emits structured events for the SLO toolkit to consume.

Design notes and motivation: We designed branching heuristics as a small rule-engine (configurable) rather than a black-box model to keep behavior auditable and debuggable for on-call teams. The initial rule set focuses on common production scenarios observed in postmortems: cache invalidation, downstream latency, DB error bursts, and partial region failures. Each rule maps to a short checklist fragment with measurable verification steps.

Checklist for this PR (validated in staging):
- [x] UX component built and tested in chrome/firefox/chromium-based apps
- [x] Backend rule-engine + API endpoints with feature-flag gating
- [x] Diagnostic snapshot hook integrated with incident-bot ephemeral storage
- [x] Safety gating and RBAC checks wired to existing SSO policy
- [x] E2E integration test that simulates an SLO breach and exercises branching
- [x] Docs (oncall playbook + admin feature flag guide)

Commits summary: see commits field for short messages; highlights include the interactive frontend, the rule-engine, and a safety/consent middleware.

Changed areas (high-level): UI surface in web app (interactive checklist), backend rule engine and API, incident timeline logging, ephemeral diagnostics plumbing, k8s job templates for safe remediation runner, docs and admin flags. Small code changes were made to the SLO toolkit event schema so it can consume decision-hint payloads.

Review conversation (abridged):
- Samir: "Solid UX—can we make the confidence score threshold editable per-org?"
- Elena: "Yes, added an admin flag and default to 0.7; documented in admin guide."
- Lena: "Concern: automated mitigation runner needs stronger rate-limiting; please ensure team-level quotas."
- Elena: "Added middleware that enforces per-team quotas and an audit event for every run; added tests."
- Marta: "Please add an integration test that runs a simulated rollback and verifies timeline entries."
- Elena: "Added e2e test and marked the PR ready for squash merge."

CI summary: initial CI run had a flaky frontend test (timeout) and one lint failure; after fixes and a re-run, all checks passed. The pipeline includes unit tests, lint, integration E2E in staging, and a canary smoke test.

Merge outcome: merged via squash. Feature is feature-flagged off by default in production; rollout plan in docs: enable for a single SRE team, collect usage and false-positive rates, then broader rollout.

Notes for oncall and SREs: The rule mapping and confidence thresholds live in deploy/config/incident-rules.yaml; avoid manual edits in prod without code review. If you spot a misclassification, open ENG-8421 to tune heuristics and attach example telemetry fingerprints.
